message.content: {"alternatives":[],"likely_cause":{"claim":"Image processing jobs began failing due to the image-resizer workers being terminated by OOMKilled errors caused by memory limits being exceeded while decoding large images.","evidence_ids":["log:7","log:4","log:6","log:3"]},"missing_evidence":[],"observations":[{"claim":"The image-resizer service logs show multiple worker processes terminated due to OOMKilled errors with a 4.0 GiB memory limit.","evidence_ids":["log:7","log:4"]},{"claim":"Warnings indicate workers were using close to the 4.0 GiB memory limit while decoding large images (e.g., 191 MiB, 12800x9600 px).","evidence_ids":["log:6","log:3"]},{"claim":"The upload-gateway service reported resize failures mostly for source images above 150 MiB, with 63 failures out of 1204 jobs in the last 30 minutes.","evidence_ids":["log:10"]},{"claim":"An upload was accepted for a large image (218 MiB, 14000x10500 px) shortly before the failures began.","evidence_ids":["log:2"]},{"claim":"The image-resizer service enabled codec pipeline v4 at 100 percent rollout, which decodes full-resolution frames before downsampling, potentially increasing memory usage.","evidence_ids":["log:1","log:9"]}],"outcome":"supported","suggested_checks":["Check memory usage and limits on image-resizer workers during large image processing.","Review recent changes related to codec pipeline v4 rollout and its memory impact.","Inspect upload-gateway logs for patterns in failed resize jobs related to image size."]}
